Messages.Author: Judith Cookson Grunberger
Messages.Body:
[rant on]

Is it me or is the DC smoking very large crack rocks? They are doing some
kind of very hard drugs, methinks. What were they thinking when they came
up with these tournament rules? Sigh...

>1. Vampire: The Eternal Struggle tournament decks may be built using
>cards from the Jyhad and Vampire: The Eternal Struggle card sets. If you
>choose to use cards from both sets, between forty and sixty percent of
>your library should be from the Jyhad set. If you use cards from both
>sets, read the rules on marked decks (Section 5).

Ok, so if the only VTES cards I have in my deck are from Dark Soveriegns,
will that be considered marking my deck? I'd hazard a "yes" on that one.
Also, in order to get 40% (minimum) of my deck to be from VTES, I'd have
to play a Dark Soveriegns clan with Dark Soveriegns disciplines. Whoops.
Guess they did screw over Jyhad players after all.

>2. The crypt must contain a minimum of 12 (twelve) vampire cards. The
>crypt can be made up of vampires from the Jyhad or Vampire: The Eternal
>Struggle card sets, but not both. There is no maximum on the number of
>vampires that can be in your crypt. The library can contain a minimum of
>60 (sixty) cards and maximum of 80 (eighty) cards total.

Nixes that "mixed decks will be allowed in tournaments" proclamation by
WoTC. And if there are 4-5 players per table, what happened to the built
in deck limitations? I'd say there could be 40-90 cards per deck. I can
sort of see the upper limit of 80, since it would be a pain to take 10
cards out of your deck every time you switched from a 5 player game to a
4 player game, but where in hell did they get that lower limit of 60?
As far as I can tell, the lower limit is 40, with an *optional* 10 cards
for every additional player in the game. Hmmmmmmm.

>3. The Restricted List:
>
>No more than 2 (two) of each of the cards on the Restricted List (by card
>title) is allowed in a Vampire: The Eternal Struggle tournament deck. If
>more than 2 (two) of any individual card from the Restricted List is found
>in a player's deck, that will be interpreted by the Judge as a Declaration
>of Forfeiture. The Restricted List may be modified by the Director of the
>Duelists' Convocation as necessary.

Did they just pull the number 2 right our of their collective asses?

>Vampire: The Eternal Struggle Restricted List
>
>% Ancilla Empowerment
>% Conservative Agitation
>% Domain Challenge
>% Earth Meld
>% Fifth Tradition: Hospitality
>% Form of Mist
>% Freak Drive
>% Kine Resources Contested
>% Majesty
>% Parity Shift
>% Sabbat Threat

Guess that TOTALLY screws political decks. Sure, it stops weenie
political decks cold, but it also eliminates any kind of legit political
deck, given that one of their main defenses, Majesty, is limited, and
also 6 (SIX!!!!!!!!!!!) vote cards. It's almost as if the DC is saying,
"OK, you can have a vote deck, but only happy friendly vote decks that
everyone loves." Um, no.

This also totally screws protean stealth-and-tap decks with the
restriction of Form of Mist and Earth Meld, and presence bleed decks with
the restriction of Majesty. Looks like Malk S&B and combat decks are about
the only options now... what BRILLIANCE!

I won't even touch Freak Drive and Fifth Tradition, which could be fixed
by card errata.

>4. The Banned List:
>
>The Vampire: The Eternal Struggle Banned List
>
>% Cunctator Motion
>% High Stakes
>% Rowan Ring
>% Monocle of Clarity
>% Stake

These almost make sense, since parlyze is kinda not in VTES, but you
know, I think people can deal with paralyze. We're not brain-dead morons. I
guess that screws my friend Todd's paralyze-amaranth deck. Sorry, Todd.

>(The Wooden Stake card from Vampire: The Eternal Struggle is permissible.)

Oh, boy. Thanks millions.

I can't be the only one who is completely baffled by these rules. What
happened? I sure as hell am not going to be playing in any tournaments,
ever. Nor will I be constructing any tournament legal decks. Of the three
I have right now, I think only my Tremere Fortitude deck passes muster. My
weenie Presence-Dominate-Obfuscate deck is illegal (too many Majesties) as
is my Protean-Fortitude-Dominate combat/stealth/untap deck (too many Earth
Melds and Form of Mists, and if I had more Freak Drives, too many of those
as well)

I think this is a good time to tell my friends (some of whom play with a
four-card limit) that now is a good time to get reeeeeal mad. And maybe
to ditch their four-cards, 'cause WoTC is obviously completely insane.

[rant off]

Judy

The funny thing about the restriction of voting is that supposedly
DS is going to be highly political. Right now there is no reason to play
a political deck, so unless DS pumps up voting big time, no one is going to
do it. This is of course just talking under tourney rules.

4 card limit right now? (This include my group btw.) Personally, I'd
rather play no limits (even though I have, far and away, the smallest card
collection, so the 4 limit helps me). However, the 2 card limit on the
cards seems rediculous. I think either something along the lines of 10%, or
a higher number (4 to 8) would have been better. (Assuming the DT doesn't
want to make all the needed rules changes to fix the problems.)

rules. I can't picture it. The funny thing is that the DC had 2 ways to
make people happy; go with a 4 card limit, or go with no limits. They did
neither, and now no one is happy.

decks nixed. So now rather than three basic decks, we have two, with
votes serving as just "spice".

of Jyhad (Jyhad went through at least 3 versions: Alpha, Beta, and Gamma).
So to strike one word from the rulebook (any *other* Methuselah) WotC has
rolled the basic game structure back an entire playtest version!

Certainly you could make an interesting game out of a combat vs bleed
contest with vote spicing. Still, voting adds great flavor to the game
and I think there are excellent reasons the game evolved to have a much
larger role for voting. In any case, backtraking would take a lot of work
- Toreadors need something else to do, you need some way of introducing
more unpredictability into votes now that vote enhancers/influencers
aren't worth putting in, etc.

For me, Jyhad without vote decks is like cooking without spices - edible,
but I think I'll have something else. The only reason I would play in a
tournament is to make a point about Dragonsbreath Rounds or Taste of
Vitae, the remaining (IMO) broken cards (which get a lot worse without
S:CE,) or Pulled Fangs, broken under the new aggro rules.

Restricting S:CE has some pretty severe effects too. The cards in
question ARE too good, but you need some defense against combat monsters
with rush, and defenses were already somewhat sparse against Brujah with
additional strike. With these rules it would take specialist decks to
deal with them.

It's getting very hard to see a good future for this game if the producers
of the game make such major changes to the game to avoid some very
reasonable errata or to stick to dysfunctional interpretations of the
rules.

in both competitive and friendly play, needs to be found. It's probably that

1) Garfield made a major booboo allowing a deck style (all vote) that both

major balance problem.

pushing, but the DT allowed it. Why start being a stickler for written

About the 40% card mix, to me there is only one solution that the
DC could easily adopt without much hassle:
Delete the part concerning card sleeves saying that a player can be
forced to unsleeve his/her cards.
This way if I have a mix of VTES and Jyhad, I can double pack all
the cards in sleeves (could even use all my extra vamppires as the backs).

Another posibility is to let players proxy cards that they own (to
bad there isn't a mostly blank card like the MtG plains) so that card backs
are the same.
Or some sort of box that would hide the card backs before drawn.
(Granted that your opponents might eventually figure out a pattern,
but at least its better then having to buy VTES if you don't want to.
Besides, you could probably pick up a little bit of variety in you
commons if you had to.)
Of course, a card trade in plan would be far and away the best,
but it seems like this won't happen.

This problem seems much more far reaching then the card limit thing
because this is not a "quick fix" deal, like the card limit is. (Ok, not
really easy for WotC/DC but atleast its only rules changes.)
Has anyone come up with a decent way of solving this problem?

>manage to within the time limit, but some guy at another table would have
>scored more vp's than me.

I read this, and started composing a rebuttal in my head. This rebuttal
was going to point out that in Magic, there is this very difference between
many peoples' private play (where people mess around with Thallid decks or
Purple Blast decks or whatever), and tournament play (where you try to reduce
the average number of turns in which you kill your opponent), and yet,
this difference has not stopped the tournament rules from becoming, in
many areas, the default rules for private play.

But you know what? I've always hated the fact that the DC rules became
standard. In fact, I routinely try to prod people into ignoring those
rules, or at least coming up with house variants, particularly during
discussions on the merits of Type I vs. Type II.

What you have to realize is that tournaments are, by definition, run under
a time limit. A convention says it has a tournament for such-and-such a
game, and a certain time limit is alloted, and everything has to be
finished within that limit. (Some private groups might run one game a week
for a couple of months and call that a tournament, but that's really more of a
league.) An environment where everyone wants to finish in roughly two hours
is obviously going to be different than an environment were you can just
sit down, enjoy yourselves, and play a game of VTES. In other words, it will
not surprise me at all if tournament rules get largely ignored by VTES groups
that are not practicing for tournaments, regardless of what the tournament
rules happen to be.

Questions like whether untapping cards should cost blood are general gameplay
issues, not issues specific to jumping into a limited-time environment, and
this, I believe, is why the DC doesn't get involved with those issues.
Tournament rules are meant to oversee tournaments, not private play, and that's
why they're called tournament rules.

I have never run into one of these degenerate weenie vote decks that has been
unstoppable, although I believe they must exist since they are such a hot
topic of discussion. Because I have no experience with such a deck, my
comments may be off track, but I think that the cards everyone seems to have a
problem with are KRC's and CA's. Possibly the same restriction should be
added to these votes as is on Sabbat Threats and other powerful votes: they
can only be called by a prince or justicar.

I believe that the rules should be written to allow the greatest number of
viable strategies, even including weenie vote decks. Possibly this change
would take the unfair edge away from the weenie vote deck while still leaving
it as a viable strategy. A low cost vampire couldn't start throwing out KRC's
as soon as it comes under your control: it would have to call and pass a
Praxis Seizure first. This means that the methusalah couldn't pack so many

the weenie voter would have some weenie's and a few princes, and would have to
protect the princes from Rushes and Intercepters.

I think that ruling out vote pushing would be a huge mistake, since it would
pretty much require presence for a voting deck. My Nosferatu voting deck,
which doesn't win a lot but is a blast to play, would never even be a factor
at all if I couldn't push my own votes. I think we can find a solution to put

The difference here is that if you play the private play Magic deck that is
slow against the high speed tournament winner, the high speed tourney deck
will win, and therefore, a winning deck in a tournament is representative of a
winning deck in Magic. However, if the slower acting Jyhad/V:TES deck is
played against the high speed tourney Jyhad/V:TES deck, it is quite possible
that the slower deck will beat the high speed one every time in a private play
environment. Therefore, the winning deck in a tournament is NOT
representative of the best winning deck of Jyhad, and I believe the point of a
tournament is that the best player/deck wins. I'm not griping about tourney
rules; I know it would never work without a time limit. I'm just saying this
is the difference between Magic and Jyhad/V:TES, and this is one of the
reasons why I believe the tourney rules will not be played in the private play
environments.

Peace Dave,

You are playing an unusual deck (kind of like a Blue "blast" deck in Mt$). Clans
with Presense are supposed to be the strong political ones, those with Dominate
the big bleeders, those with Auspex the interceptors, etc. You are playing a clan
that isn't well suited toward politics (kind of like building a Brujah S&B deck).
Vote pushing terribly unbalances the game towards all-PA decks. As the rules
rules currently stand, politics isn't very political; it tends to boil down to who
has the most PAs in hand when the vote is called [no, this isn't ALWAYS true, but
it is more often then not]. One PA card per Meth per vote would make politics more
political (more negotiation/diplomacy). Yes, I realize that some people don't like
the idea that their political deck would have to cooperate to get votes to pass,
but it is a much more balance and playable solution than "I've got seven vote cards
in my hand. You lose."

a clan that is weak in politics means that you will do poorly against a political

a) It was 6-card limits, not 2.

cards won't stop KRC decks (although there is some disputation on how

When someone is concerned with slowing a Meth soon to be their predator,
that's normal. When the whole table drops the predator-prey relationships
to put the brakes on somebody, that's abnormal. That's an arrangement
typical of multiplayer games, and tends to lead to stalemates. Presumably
avoiding the "stop the leader" tendency is the reason Garfield put
predator-prey into the game.
